Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Plot shapes their sequence and relationships.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 4. Which element is a work's explored underlying idea?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-04 · easy · remember

- A. Theme
- B. Character
- C. Setting
- D. Plot

Answer: **A**. Theme concerns its larger significance.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Theme concerns its larger significance.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 5. A narrator tells their own experience using I. Which viewpoint?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-05 · easy · remember

- A. Third-person omniscient
- B. Second person
- C. Third-person limited
- D. First person

Answer: **D**. The speaker participates in the narrative.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: The speaker participates in the narrative.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 6. A narrative addresses the main figure as you. Which viewpoint?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-06 · easy · remember

- A. First person
- B. Third-person omniscient
- C. Second person
- D. Third-person limited

Answer: **C**. Second person directly addresses a participant.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Second person directly addresses a participant.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 7. A narrator uses she but enters only one character's mind. Which viewpoint?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-07 · medium · understand

- A. Third-person limited
- B. Second person
- C. Third-person omniscient
- D. First person

Answer: **A**. Access is limited to that consciousness.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Access is limited to that consciousness.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 8. A narrator presents several characters' private thoughts. Which viewpoint?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-08 · medium · understand

- A. Third-person omniscient
- B. First person
- C. Third-person limited
- D. Second person

Answer: **A**. Omniscient narration can range across minds.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Omniscient narration can range across minds.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 9. 'Damp earth smelled sharp after the rain' emphasizes what?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-09 · medium · understand

- A. Sensory imagery
- B. Metaphor
- C. Concrete detail
- D. Dialogue

Answer: **A**. The wording evokes sensory experience.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: The wording evokes sensory experience.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 10. Characters exchange spoken lines. Which technique is used?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-10 · medium · understand

- A. Metaphor
- B. Dialogue
- C. Concrete detail
- D. Sensory imagery

Answer: **B**. Dialogue presents speech.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Dialogue presents speech.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 11. 'Her hope was a small lamp' uses what?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-11 · medium · understand

- A. Dialogue
- B. Metaphor
- C. Sensory imagery
- D. Concrete detail

Answer: **B**. The comparison is direct rather than literal.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: The comparison is direct rather than literal.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 12. 'A chipped blue mug' replaces 'an object.' What has improved?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-12 · medium · understand

- A. Sensory imagery
- B. Concrete detail
- C. Metaphor
- D. Dialogue

Answer: **B**. Specific description makes the object imaginable.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Specific description makes the object imaginable.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 13. Background information establishes a story's situation. What is this?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-13 · medium · understand

- A. Resolution
- B. Climax
- C. Exposition
- D. Rising action

Answer: **C**. Exposition introduces necessary context.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Exposition introduces necessary context.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 14. Complications intensify the central struggle. What stage is this?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-14 · medium · understand

- A. Rising action
- B. Resolution
- C. Exposition
- D. Climax

Answer: **A**. Rising action develops tension.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Rising action develops tension.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 15. A decisive confrontation turns the struggle. What stage is this?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-15 · medium · understand

- A. Exposition
- B. Climax
- C. Rising action
- D. Resolution

Answer: **B**. The climax concentrates the turning conflict.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: The climax concentrates the turning conflict.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 16. The aftermath shows consequences and remaining conditions. What stage is this?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-16 · medium · understand

- A. Rising action
- B. Climax
- C. Resolution
- D. Exposition

Answer: **C**. Resolution follows the decisive events.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Resolution follows the decisive events.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 17. A draft labels a character generous but shows no behavior. What revision helps?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Maintain viewpoint consistency
- B. Remove an unearned coincidence
- C. Use selective implication
- D. Reveal through action

Answer: **D**. Actions can make the quality credible.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Actions can make the quality credible.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 18. A limited narrator suddenly states everyone's hidden thoughts without transition. What needs review?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-18 · hard · analyze

- A. Remove an unearned coincidence
- B. Maintain viewpoint consistency
- C. Reveal through action
- D. Use selective implication

Answer: **B**. The narrative's access has changed without explanation.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: The narrative's access has changed without explanation.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 19. A central problem vanishes through an unexplained lucky event. What should be revised?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Use selective implication
- B. Maintain viewpoint consistency
- C. Reveal through action
- D. Remove an unearned coincidence

Answer: **D**. Resolution should arise credibly from the narrative.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Resolution should arise credibly from the narrative.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 20. A scene explains every feeling several times after already showing it. What may strengthen it?

ID: KAT135-ENGLISH-048-20 · hard · analyze

- A. Maintain viewpoint consistency
- B. Reveal through action
- C. Use selective implication
- D. Remove an unearned coincidence

Answer: **C**. Readers can infer from well-chosen details.

Objective: Demonstrate Creative Writing: Readers can infer from well-chosen details.

Sources: [current-creative](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/MALIKHAING-PAGSULAT-1.pdf)

### 19. May marahas na tauhan ang akda. Bakit hindi agad masasabi na sinasang-ayunan siya ng may-akda?

## Araling Panlipunan / Social Studies / Philippine History

Catalogue grades: GRADE_7. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. Philippine independence from Spain was proclaimed on which date?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-01 · easy · remember

- A. June 19, 1861.
- B. June 12, 1898.
- C. July 4, 1946.
- D. February 25, 1986.

Answer: **B**. The declaration occurred in June 1898.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: The declaration occurred in June 1898.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 2. Where was the 1898 declaration made?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-02 · easy · remember

- A. Dapitan, Zamboanga.
- B. Malolos, Bulacan.
- C. Kawit, Cavite.
- D. Cebu City.

Answer: **C**. Kawit was the declaration site.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Kawit was the declaration site.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 3. Who proclaimed independence in Kawit?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-03 · easy · remember

- A. Manuel Quezon.
- B. Jose Rizal.
- C. Apolinario Mabini.
- D. Emilio Aguinaldo.

Answer: **D**. Aguinaldo led the proclamation.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Aguinaldo led the proclamation.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 4. Which organization pursued revolutionary independence from Spain?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-04 · easy · remember

- A. United Nations.
- B. ASEAN.
- C. Katipunan.
- D. League of Nations.

Answer: **C**. The Katipunan organized revolutionary resistance.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: The Katipunan organized revolutionary resistance.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 5. Which country recognized Philippine independence on July 4, 1946?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-05 · easy · remember

- A. Portugal.
- B. Spain.
- C. United States.
- D. Japan.

Answer: **C**. American colonial rule formally ended with recognition in 1946.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: American colonial rule formally ended with recognition in 1946.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 6. What is a historical primary source?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-06 · easy · remember

- A. A contemporaneous diary.
- B. A recent historical novel.
- C. A modern textbook summary.
- D. An unsourced online summary.

Answer: **A**. A diary can directly document its period.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: A diary can directly document its period.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 7. A historian compares two eyewitness accounts. Why?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-07 · medium · understand

- A. To ensure both use identical wording.
- B. To prove every witness is impartial.
- C. To avoid examining evidence.
- D. To assess agreements, differences and perspective.

Answer: **D**. Accounts can differ in access and viewpoint.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Accounts can differ in access and viewpoint.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 8. Which came first?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-08 · medium · apply

- A. The 1935 Commonwealth.
- B. The 1898 declaration.
- C. The 1946 recognition.
- D. The 1986 People Power Revolution.

Answer: **B**. Chronology places 1898 before the other dates.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Chronology places 1898 before the other dates.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 9. Why distinguish declaration from international recognition?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-09 · medium · understand

- A. Declarations never concern independence.
- B. Recognition erases earlier events.
- C. They always happen on the same day.
- D. They are different historical and political events.

Answer: **D**. A proclaimed claim and its recognition are distinct.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: A proclaimed claim and its recognition are distinct.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 10. A colonial official describes a revolt as disorder. What should be considered?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-10 · medium · apply

- A. The title alone proves neutrality.
- B. The official's institutional perspective.
- C. Only the handwriting matters.
- D. The account must be entirely false.

Answer: **B**. Institutional position can shape interpretation.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Institutional position can shape interpretation.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 11. A photograph lacks a date and location. What is needed?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-11 · medium · understand

- A. Provenance and contextual verification.
- B. An attractive frame only.
- C. A longer caption invented by the researcher.
- D. An assumption that it shows any chosen event.

Answer: **A**. Context is needed to identify what it documents.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Context is needed to identify what it documents.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 12. Why study local oral histories?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-12 · medium · apply

- A. They never require corroboration.
- B. They are automatically infallible.
- C. They replace every written source.
- D. They can preserve experiences absent from official records.

Answer: **D**. Oral accounts broaden available perspectives.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Oral accounts broaden available perspectives.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 13. What does a historical timeline help establish?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-13 · medium · understand

- A. The accuracy of every quotation.
- B. The moral worth of every participant.
- C. Sequence and temporal relationships.
- D. Automatic proof of causation.

Answer: **C**. A timeline organizes events by time.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: A timeline organizes events by time.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 14. How should a historical novel be used?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-14 · medium · apply

- A. As fiction that may require independent factual checking.
- B. As evidence that no archives exist.
- C. As unquestionable documentary proof.
- D. As the only source for every date.

Answer: **A**. Fiction can use history without documenting every detail.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Fiction can use history without documenting every detail.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 15. Why identify who created a document and for whom?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-15 · medium · understand

- A. Only document length matters.
- B. Authors never have purposes.
- C. Audience determines every date automatically.
- D. Purpose and audience influence its content.

Answer: **D**. Source criticism examines context and intended use.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Source criticism examines context and intended use.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 16. Which is historical continuity?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-16 · medium · apply

- A. One event occurs once.
- B. A practice persists across political changes.
- C. Every institution changes overnight.
- D. An archive closes temporarily.

Answer: **B**. Continuity concerns features that endure.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Continuity concerns features that endure.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 17. Two documents give different casualty totals. What is the strongest response?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Compare definitions, methods, dates and coverage.
- B. Discard every source permanently.
- C. Average them without examination.
- D. Choose the larger because it is dramatic.

Answer: **A**. Differences may reflect counting scope and evidence.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Differences may reflect counting scope and evidence.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 18. A source written decades later describes an earlier event. What limitation matters?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. It cannot contain any useful information.
- B. Memory and later interpretation may influence the account.
- C. Its author must have witnessed every event.
- D. It is automatically contemporary evidence.

Answer: **B**. Retrospective accounts require contextual evaluation.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Retrospective accounts require contextual evaluation.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 19. An earlier protest is followed by reform. Why is chronology alone insufficient to prove causation?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Other actors and conditions may have contributed.
- B. Reforms have no causes.
- C. Earlier events can never influence later ones.
- D. Dates always establish motives.

Answer: **A**. Causal explanation requires more than sequence.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Causal explanation requires more than sequence.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

### 20. A textbook tells only leaders' experiences. What addition broadens historical understanding?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-29-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. A replacement of all evidence with opinion.
- B. Only a longer list of rulers.
- C. Evidence from ordinary people and marginalized groups.
- D. A decorative map without labels.

Answer: **C**. Multiple social perspectives improve historical coverage.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasaysayan ng Pilipinas: Multiple social perspectives improve historical coverage.

Sources: [history](https://history.house.gov/Exhibitions-and-Publications/APA/Historical-essays/Exclusion-and-Empire/The-Philippines/), [historyph](https://pvao.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Philippine-History.pdf)

- D. Cultural exchange

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-066-02 · easy · remember

- A. Maritime trade
- B. Cultural exchange
- C. River-valley settlement
- D. Colonial rule

### 3. Religious ideas and writing spread through contact. Which process?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-066-03 · easy · remember

- A. Maritime trade
- B. River-valley settlement
- C. Colonial rule
- D. Cultural exchange

Answer: **D**. Interaction can transmit cultural practices.

Sources: [current-seasia](https://www.britannica.com/place/Southeast-Asia), [current-asean](https://www.britannica.com/topic/ASEAN)

### 4. A foreign state governs a territory without local sovereignty. Which relationship?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-066-04 · easy · remember

- A. River-valley settlement
- B. Cultural exchange
- C. Maritime trade
- D. Colonial rule

Answer: **D**. External political control characterizes colonial rule.

- A. No; preparedness has no value.
- B. No; exposure, vulnerability and capacity must all be considered.
- C. Yes; shelters remove the hazard itself.
- D. Yes; maps cannot show danger.

Answer: **B**. Protective capacity can reduce but not eliminate risk.

Objective: Demonstrate Heograpiya: Protective capacity can reduce but not eliminate risk.

Sources: [geography](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/ARALING-PANLIPUNAN-GRADES-4-7.pdf)

### 18. A population grows while land area stays fixed. What happens to density?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-30-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. It increases.
- B. It becomes rainfall.
- C. It decreases.
- D. It must remain unchanged.

Answer: **A**. More people occupy the same area.

Objective: Demonstrate Heograpiya: More people occupy the same area.

Sources: [geography](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/ARALING-PANLIPUNAN-GRADES-4-7.pdf)

### 19. Why compare several map layers before locating a school?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-30-19 · hard · analyze

- A. One layer always answers every question.
- B. Colors alone determine safety.
- C. Hazards, access and settlement needs interact.
- D. Population information has no relevance.

Answer: **C**. Site decisions require multiple spatial factors.

Objective: Demonstrate Heograpiya: Site decisions require multiple spatial factors.

Sources: [geography](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/ARALING-PANLIPUNAN-GRADES-4-7.pdf)

### 20. A flat world map makes a high-latitude region look very large. What should be checked?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-30-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. Only the font.
- B. The projection's area distortion.
- C. Whether the region has roads.
- D. The number of map folds.

Answer: **B**. Projection choice can misrepresent relative area.

Objective: Demonstrate Heograpiya: Projection choice can misrepresent relative area.

Sources: [geography](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/ARALING-PANLIPUNAN-GRADES-4-7.pdf)

## Araling Panlipunan / Social Studies / Economics & the National Economy

Catalogue grades: GRADE_9, GRADE_10. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. What is scarcity?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-01 · easy · remember

- A. Limited resources relative to wants.
- B. A fixed price for all goods.
- C. The absence of every resource.
- D. Unlimited production.

Answer: **A**. Resources cannot satisfy every competing want.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Resources cannot satisfy every competing want.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 2. Opportunity cost is what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-02 · easy · remember

- A. All money ever earned.
- B. The best alternative forgone.
- C. A business's logo.
- D. Only a product's tax.

Answer: **B**. A choice sacrifices its next-best alternative.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: A choice sacrifices its next-best alternative.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 3. Demand involves willingness and what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-03 · easy · remember

- A. Ability to buy.
- B. Ability to advertise only.
- C. Population size alone.
- D. Government ownership.

Answer: **A**. Effective demand requires purchasing ability.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Effective demand requires purchasing ability.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 4. Supply concerns what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-04 · easy · remember

- A. Only buyers' wishes.
- B. Quantities sellers offer at different prices.
- C. Only household leisure.
- D. Every free natural resource.

Answer: **B**. Supply describes sellers' price-quantity relationship.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Supply describes sellers' price-quantity relationship.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 5. Equilibrium occurs when what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-05 · easy · remember

- A. Every product is free.
- B. No buyer has wants.
- C. All firms have identical costs.
- D. Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

Answer: **D**. Equilibrium balances planned purchases and sales.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Equilibrium balances planned purchases and sales.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 6. A consumer is primarily someone who does what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-06 · easy · remember

- A. Uses goods or services.
- B. Only prints currency.
- C. Only owns factories.
- D. Only writes laws.

Answer: **A**. Consumption involves using outputs.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Consumption involves using outputs.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 7. A pupil chooses studying over a movie. What is the opportunity cost?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-07 · medium · understand

- A. The price of all films.
- B. The forgone movie experience.
- C. The study room's entire value.
- D. Every future school expense.

Answer: **B**. The movie is the sacrificed alternative.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: The movie is the sacrificed alternative.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 8. Other things equal, a price increase usually does what to quantity demanded?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-08 · medium · apply

- A. Eliminates the demand curve.
- B. Decreases it.
- C. Increases it necessarily.
- D. Leaves it infinite.

Answer: **B**. This is movement along a downward-sloping demand curve.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: This is movement along a downward-sloping demand curve.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 9. Other things equal, higher product prices often encourage sellers to do what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-09 · medium · understand

- A. Stop all production automatically.
- B. Reduce supply to zero necessarily.
- C. Ignore revenue permanently.
- D. Offer more output.

Answer: **D**. Higher prices can make additional output worthwhile.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Higher prices can make additional output worthwhile.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 10. At a price below equilibrium, what commonly results?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-10 · medium · apply

- A. No demand.
- B. An automatic surplus.
- C. Unlimited supply.
- D. A shortage.

Answer: **D**. Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 11. At a price above equilibrium, what commonly results?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-11 · medium · understand

- A. No sellers.
- B. A shortage necessarily.
- C. A surplus.
- D. Zero inventories always.

Answer: **C**. Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 12. Income rises for buyers of a normal good. What shift is expected?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-12 · medium · apply

- A. Demand must decrease.
- B. Supply becomes a vertical line necessarily.
- C. Demand increases.
- D. Price becomes zero.

Answer: **C**. Normal-good demand rises with income.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Normal-good demand rises with income.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 13. Which is a production input?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-13 · medium · understand

- A. A customer's receipt only.
- B. Finished consumption alone.
- C. Labor.
- D. A brand slogan only.

Answer: **C**. Labor contributes to producing goods and services.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Labor contributes to producing goods and services.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 14. A firm sells goods for ₱500 with total cost ₱350. Profit?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-14 · medium · apply

- A. ₱350.
- B. ₱500.
- C. ₱150.
- D. ₱850.

Answer: **C**. Profit equals revenue minus cost.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Profit equals revenue minus cost.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 15. Which best describes a budget?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-15 · medium · understand

- A. A plan allocating income among uses.
- B. A guarantee of unlimited spending.
- C. A list of prices with no income information.
- D. Only a debt collector's notice.

Answer: **A**. A budget coordinates available funds and planned spending.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: A budget coordinates available funds and planned spending.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 16. Why can savings support future spending?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-16 · medium · apply

- A. They guarantee every investment gains.
- B. They always double immediately.
- C. They eliminate every expense.
- D. They set aside current resources for later use.

Answer: **D**. Saving transfers purchasing capacity across time.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Saving transfers purchasing capacity across time.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 17. A drought reduces harvest while demand stays unchanged. What market tendency is expected?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Lower supply and upward price pressure.
- B. Demand automatically disappears.
- C. No possible price change.
- D. More supply and lower price necessarily.

Answer: **A**. A supply reduction can raise equilibrium price.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: A supply reduction can raise equilibrium price.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 18. A price rises and sales fall. Does this alone prove demand shifted left?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. Yes; every fall in sales is a demand shift.
- B. No; it may be movement along demand caused by a supply change.
- C. No; demand curves cannot exist.
- D. Yes; supply never changes.

Answer: **B**. Observed price and quantity require distinguishing shifts from movements.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Observed price and quantity require distinguishing shifts from movements.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 19. A factory's smoke harms nearby residents. What economic issue is illustrated?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-19 · hard · analyze

- A. A guaranteed public good.
- B. A private benefit only.
- C. A negative externality.
- D. An opportunity with no social cost.

Answer: **C**. Some costs fall on parties outside the transaction.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Some costs fall on parties outside the transaction.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 20. Why is a low price not sufficient to establish best value?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-31-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. Quality never affects usefulness.
- B. Future costs cannot occur.
- C. The highest price always gives best value.
- D. Quality, durability and total ownership costs also matter.

Answer: **D**. Value depends on benefits and costs beyond purchase price.

Objective: Demonstrate Ekonomiks: Value depends on benefits and costs beyond purchase price.

Sources: [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

## Araling Panlipunan / Social Studies / Government & Citizenship

Catalogue grades: GRADE_7, GRADE_8, GRADE_9, GRADE_10. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. Under the Philippine Constitution, sovereignty resides in whom?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-01 · easy · remember

- A. The people.
- B. Only the courts.
- C. Only the President.
- D. Foreign governments.

Answer: **A**. Article II locates sovereignty in the people.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Article II locates sovereignty in the people.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 2. Which branch primarily enacts national laws?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-02 · easy · remember

- A. Judicial.
- B. Legislative.
- C. Civil service alone.
- D. Executive.

Answer: **B**. Congress exercises legislative power.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Congress exercises legislative power.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 3. Which branch primarily executes laws?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-03 · easy · remember

- A. Legislative.
- B. Constitutional commissions collectively.
- C. Executive.
- D. Judicial.

Answer: **C**. Executive power is vested in the President.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Executive power is vested in the President.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 4. Which branch interprets laws in deciding cases?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-04 · easy · remember

- A. Judicial.
- B. Local business associations.
- C. Legislative.
- D. Executive.

Answer: **A**. Courts exercise judicial power.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Courts exercise judicial power.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 5. What is the basic law of the Philippines?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-05 · easy · remember

- A. The Constitution.
- B. A private club rule.
- C. Every social-media post.
- D. A newspaper editorial.

Answer: **A**. The Constitution is the fundamental legal framework.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: The Constitution is the fundamental legal framework.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 6. What is suffrage?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-06 · easy · remember

- A. An obligation to join one party.
- B. The right to own every property.
- C. A court sentence.
- D. The right to vote, subject to constitutional qualifications.

Answer: **D**. Suffrage concerns participation through voting.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Suffrage concerns participation through voting.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 7. Why are government powers divided among branches?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-07 · medium · understand

- A. To make all offices identical.
- B. To distribute authority and enable checks and balances.
- C. To remove accountability.
- D. To abolish every law.

Answer: **B**. Separated powers help restrain concentration of authority.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Separated powers help restrain concentration of authority.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 8. Which action illustrates civic participation?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-08 · medium · apply

- A. Selling another person's vote.
- B. Fabricating a government notice.
- C. Destroying public records.
- D. Attending a lawful public consultation.

Answer: **D**. Consultation allows public involvement in decisions.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Consultation allows public involvement in decisions.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 9. Which protects a person accused of an offense?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-09 · medium · understand

- A. Automatic punishment based on rumor.
- B. Denial of every hearing.
- C. Presumption of innocence until guilt is proved.
- D. Conviction by popularity poll.

Answer: **C**. The Bill of Rights provides the presumption of innocence.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: The Bill of Rights provides the presumption of innocence.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 10. Why is due process important?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-10 · medium · apply

- A. It eliminates the need for evidence.
- B. It guarantees everyone wins every case.
- C. It guards against arbitrary deprivation of rights.
- D. It gives officials unlimited power.

Answer: **C**. Fair legal procedures constrain arbitrary action.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Fair legal procedures constrain arbitrary action.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 11. Who heads a Philippine city or municipality's executive administration?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-11 · medium · understand

- A. A private school principal.
- B. The Chief Justice.
- C. A national senator.
- D. The mayor.

Answer: **D**. The mayor leads the local executive.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: The mayor leads the local executive.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 12. Which is responsible citizenship?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-12 · medium · apply

- A. Ignoring all public obligations.
- B. Following lawful rules while using lawful means to seek reform.
- C. Buying votes.
- D. Believing every anonymous accusation.

Answer: **B**. Citizens can comply and participate in democratic change.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Citizens can comply and participate in democratic change.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 13. Why verify a government announcement's official source?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-13 · medium · understand

- A. To avoid acting on forged or outdated information.
- B. Because spelling alone proves authenticity.
- C. Because all unofficial discussion is illegal.
- D. Only to count its images.

Answer: **A**. Provenance and currency help establish authenticity.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Provenance and currency help establish authenticity.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 14. What does public accountability require?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-14 · medium · apply

- A. Public funds become personal money.
- B. Officials answer for the use of authority and resources.
- C. Citizens may never ask questions.
- D. Officials are above every rule.

Answer: **B**. Public office carries responsibility to the people.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Public office carries responsibility to the people.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 15. Which illustrates equal protection in principle?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-15 · medium · understand

- A. All relevant differences must be ignored.
- B. Friends of officials always receive exemptions.
- C. Only wealthy people receive hearings.
- D. Comparable cases receive legally justified consistent treatment.

Answer: **D**. Equal protection bars unjustified discriminatory treatment.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Equal protection bars unjustified discriminatory treatment.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 16. A citizen disagrees with a policy. Which response fits democratic participation?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-16 · medium · apply

- A. Forge official records.
- B. Present evidence and petition through lawful channels.
- C. Threaten anyone who disagrees.
- D. Assume disagreement itself is forbidden.

Answer: **B**. Lawful expression and petition support participation.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Lawful expression and petition support participation.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 17. A popular majority wants punishment without a hearing. What constitutional concern arises?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Due process is not displaced merely by popularity.
- B. Rights apply only to officials.
- C. Courts need no evidence when opinions are strong.
- D. Popularity automatically establishes guilt.

Answer: **A**. Constitutional protections constrain majoritarian impulses.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Constitutional protections constrain majoritarian impulses.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 18. An official approves a contract benefiting their own business. What should be examined?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. Whether the contract is printed neatly.
- B. Only the business's logo.
- C. Conflict of interest and applicable accountability rules.
- D. Whether the official has many followers.

Answer: **C**. Private interests may compromise public decision-making.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Private interests may compromise public decision-making.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 19. Why cannot one isolated online quotation establish a law's current meaning?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Every short quotation is false.
- B. Only popularity determines legal meaning.
- C. The full provision, amendments and legal context matter.
- D. Laws never have context.

Answer: **C**. Legal interpretation requires the applicable authoritative text and context.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Legal interpretation requires the applicable authoritative text and context.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 20. A proposed project is legal but poorly explained to residents. What improves accountable decision-making?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-32-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. Hide all project details.
- B. Replace evidence with personal attacks.
- C. Claim legality removes every duty to explain.
- D. Disclose relevant information and provide meaningful consultation.

Answer: **D**. Transparency and participation improve public scrutiny.

Objective: Demonstrate Sibika at Pamahalaan: Transparency and participation improve public scrutiny.

Sources: [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

## Araling Panlipunan / Social Studies / Philippine Politics & Governance

Catalogue grades: GRADE_11. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. Which branch generally legislates national policy?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-01 · easy · remember

- D. Constitutional commissions

Answer: **C**. Congress exercises legislative authority.

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-02 · easy · remember

- A. Executive
- B. Constitutional commissions
- C. Judiciary
- D. Legislature

Answer: **A**. Executive institutions administer policy.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Executive institutions administer policy.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 3. Which branch resolves legal disputes through courts?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-03 · easy · remember

- A. Constitutional commissions
- B. Legislature
- C. Judiciary
- D. Executive

Answer: **C**. Judicial power includes adjudication.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 4. Which category includes independent constitutional bodies such as COA?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-04 · easy · remember

- A. Legislature
- B. Constitutional commissions
- C. Executive
- D. Judiciary

Answer: **B**. These bodies have defined constitutional mandates.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: These bodies have defined constitutional mandates.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 5. Officials must answer for public decisions and resources. What principle?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-05 · easy · remember

- A. Participation
- B. Transparency
- C. Rule of law
- D. Accountability

Answer: **D**. Authority carries answerability.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Authority carries answerability.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 6. Relevant public information is accessible for scrutiny. What principle?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-06 · easy · remember

- A. Participation
- B. Accountability
- C. Rule of law
- D. Transparency

Answer: **D**. Disclosure supports oversight.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Disclosure supports oversight.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 7. Residents meaningfully contribute to public consultation. What principle?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-07 · medium · understand

- A. Rule of law
- B. Participation
- C. Accountability
- D. Transparency

Answer: **B**. They take part in decision-making.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: They take part in decision-making.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 8. Public power is subject to applicable law. What principle?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-08 · medium · understand

- A. Transparency
- B. Accountability
- C. Participation
- D. Rule of law

Answer: **D**. Officials are not above legal constraints.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Officials are not above legal constraints.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 9. Different branches can restrain each other's powers. What arrangement?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-09 · medium · understand

- A. Checks and balances
- B. Conflict of interest
- C. Decentralization
- D. Public interest

Answer: **A**. Distributed authority permits reciprocal checks.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Distributed authority permits reciprocal checks.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 10. Some authority is exercised through local governments. What process?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-10 · medium · understand

- A. Public interest
- B. Decentralization
- C. Conflict of interest
- D. Checks and balances

Answer: **B**. Functions are distributed beyond the center.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Functions are distributed beyond the center.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 11. A decision prioritizes community needs over an official's private gain. What standard?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-11 · medium · understand

- A. Conflict of interest
- B. Public interest
- C. Checks and balances
- D. Decentralization

Answer: **B**. Public office should serve the public.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Public office should serve the public.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 12. An official's personal business may benefit from their decision. What issue?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-12 · medium · understand

- A. Public interest
- B. Decentralization
- C. Conflict of interest
- D. Checks and balances

Answer: **C**. Private interest may compromise public duty.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Private interest may compromise public duty.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 13. Which is the fundamental national legal framework?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-13 · medium · understand

- A. Constitution
- B. Public policy
- C. Civil society
- D. Ordinance

Answer: **A**. The Constitution structures public authority.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: The Constitution structures public authority.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 14. Which law is enacted by an authorized local legislative body?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-14 · medium · understand

- A. Civil society
- B. Constitution
- C. Public policy
- D. Ordinance

Answer: **D**. Ordinances govern within local authority.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Ordinances govern within local authority.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 15. Which term describes an organized government course of action?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-15 · medium · understand

- A. Public policy
- B. Ordinance
- C. Civil society
- D. Constitution

Answer: **A**. Policy addresses public concerns.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Policy addresses public concerns.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 16. Which sphere includes voluntary nonstate civic organizations?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-16 · medium · understand

- A. Ordinance
- B. Public policy
- C. Civil society
- D. Constitution

Answer: **C**. Civil society can participate outside government.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Civil society can participate outside government.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 17. An official claims unlimited authority because of electoral victory. What should citizens check?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Compare outcomes with policy goals
- B. Preserve constitutional rights
- C. Scrutinize evidence, not popularity alone
- D. Examine actual powers and procedures

Answer: **D**. Election does not remove legal limits.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Election does not remove legal limits.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 18. A program spends its budget but misses its objective. What evaluation is needed?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-18 · hard · analyze

- A. Scrutinize evidence, not popularity alone
- B. Compare outcomes with policy goals
- C. Preserve constitutional rights
- D. Examine actual powers and procedures

Answer: **B**. Inputs alone do not establish effectiveness.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Inputs alone do not establish effectiveness.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 19. A widely shared accusation lacks documentation. What is appropriate?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Scrutinize evidence, not popularity alone
- B. Preserve constitutional rights
- C. Compare outcomes with policy goals
- D. Examine actual powers and procedures

Answer: **A**. Public judgment should evaluate credible evidence.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Public judgment should evaluate credible evidence.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

### 20. A majority demands punishment without a hearing. What constraint matters?

ID: KAT135-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-071-20 · hard · analyze

- A. Examine actual powers and procedures
- B. Scrutinize evidence, not popularity alone
- C. Preserve constitutional rights
- D. Compare outcomes with policy goals

Answer: **C**. Popularity does not replace due process.

Objective: Demonstrate Philippine Politics & Governance: Popularity does not replace due process.

Sources: [current-worldhistory](https://openstax.org/books/world-history-volume-1/pages/3-1-early-civilizations), [constitution](https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/1987-constitution/)

## Araling Panlipunan / Social Studies / Culture & Society

Catalogue grades: GRADE_7, GRADE_8, GRADE_9, GRADE_10, GRADE_12. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. Culture includes what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-01 · easy · remember

- A. Learned meanings, practices and material objects.
- B. Only individual height.
- C. Only mountains.
- D. Only inherited eye color.

Answer: **A**. Culture includes shared learned ways of life.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Culture includes shared learned ways of life.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 2. Which is material culture?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-02 · easy · remember

- A. A language rule alone.
- B. A traditional woven basket.
- C. A social norm.
- D. A belief about respect.

Answer: **B**. The basket is a tangible cultural object.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: The basket is a tangible cultural object.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 3. Which is nonmaterial culture?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-03 · easy · remember

- A. A shared value.
- B. A house.
- C. A woven cloth.
- D. A cooking pot.

Answer: **A**. Values are intangible cultural elements.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Values are intangible cultural elements.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 4. What is socialization?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-04 · easy · remember

- A. Only physical growth.
- B. Learning social norms and roles.
- C. A change in rock type.
- D. Only population counting.

Answer: **B**. People learn society's expectations through socialization.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: People learn society's expectations through socialization.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 5. A norm is what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-05 · easy · remember

- A. A fixed gene.
- B. A geological layer.
- C. An expected pattern of behavior.
- D. A person's blood type.

Answer: **C**. Norms guide conduct in a social setting.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Norms guide conduct in a social setting.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 6. What is a social role?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-06 · easy · remember

- A. Expected behavior linked to a position.
- B. Only a building's size.
- C. A weather pattern.
- D. A person's exact height.

Answer: **A**. Roles organize social expectations.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Roles organize social expectations.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 7. Learning a local greeting before visiting demonstrates what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-07 · medium · understand

- A. Biological adaptation only.
- B. Automatic rejection of one's culture.
- C. An absence of communication.
- D. Attention to cultural context.

Answer: **D**. Greeting practices carry local meanings.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Greeting practices carry local meanings.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 8. Judging every culture only by one's own standards is what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-08 · medium · apply

- A. Statistical sampling.
- B. Cultural relativism.
- C. Ethnocentrism.
- D. Geographic latitude.

Answer: **C**. Ethnocentrism treats one's culture as the benchmark.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Ethnocentrism treats one's culture as the benchmark.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 9. Trying to understand a practice within its own setting illustrates what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-09 · medium · understand

- A. Automatic endorsement of all harm.
- B. A claim that every act is beyond criticism.
- C. Population density.
- D. Cultural relativism.

Answer: **D**. Understanding context is distinct from endorsing every practice.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Understanding context is distinct from endorsing every practice.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 10. Why can a familiar symbol have different meanings elsewhere?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-10 · medium · apply

- A. Symbols have no meaning anywhere.
- B. Every society has identical history.
- C. Meanings are shaped by cultural conventions.
- D. Objects dictate one universal interpretation.

Answer: **C**. Shared interpretation varies between cultural settings.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Shared interpretation varies between cultural settings.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 11. Which helps preserve living cultural traditions?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-11 · medium · understand

- A. Excluding the community from all decisions.
- B. Supporting community participation and transmission.
- C. Treating all practices as unchanging displays.
- D. Replacing every tradition with a stereotype.

Answer: **B**. Living traditions depend on their practitioners.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Living traditions depend on their practitioners.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 12. Why avoid saying all members of a group behave identically?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-12 · medium · apply

- A. Culture never influences behavior.
- B. All differences are genetic.
- C. Stereotypes are complete research.
- D. Groups contain internal diversity.

Answer: **D**. A group label does not describe every individual.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: A group label does not describe every individual.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 13. Language contributes to culture by doing what?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-13 · medium · understand

- A. Determining every person's intelligence.
- B. Conveying shared meanings and knowledge.
- C. Eliminating every disagreement.
- D. Preventing cultural change.

Answer: **B**. Language supports transmission of meaning.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Language supports transmission of meaning.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 14. A person is both a student and family caregiver. What does this illustrate?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-14 · medium · apply

- A. A single biological trait.
- B. No connection to society.
- C. Absence of social identity.
- D. Multiple social roles.

Answer: **D**. Individuals occupy several positions and responsibilities.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Individuals occupy several positions and responsibilities.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 15. Why can culture change over time?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-15 · medium · understand

- A. People adapt, innovate and exchange practices.
- B. Every practice is genetically fixed.
- C. Communication prevents change.
- D. Traditions cannot be learned.

Answer: **A**. Social interaction and new conditions can reshape culture.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Social interaction and new conditions can reshape culture.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 16. A community adapts a traditional design for new materials. What may this represent?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-16 · medium · apply

- A. The end of shared meaning.
- B. Proof that culture is biological only.
- C. Automatic disappearance of all tradition.
- D. Cultural continuity alongside change.

Answer: **D**. Cultural forms can persist while changing their expression.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Cultural forms can persist while changing their expression.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 17. Is understanding a practice's context the same as excusing harm?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Yes; culture removes every right.
- B. Yes; analysis forbids all criticism.
- C. No; contextual understanding can coexist with ethical evaluation.
- D. No; context is always irrelevant.

Answer: **C**. Explanation and moral endorsement are distinct tasks.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Explanation and moral endorsement are distinct tasks.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 18. A museum displays objects without community perspectives. What improves interpretation?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. Add only higher prices.
- B. Include the makers' knowledge and context.
- C. Remove every description.
- D. Assume visitors know the meanings.

Answer: **B**. Community perspectives clarify cultural significance.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Community perspectives clarify cultural significance.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 19. A survey of one urban group is labeled the culture of all Filipinos. What is the problem?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-19 · hard · analyze

- A. It ignores regional and social diversity.
- B. It includes too much context.
- C. National culture cannot be studied at all.
- D. Every urban resident is identical.

Answer: **A**. A narrow sample cannot represent all cultural variation.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: A narrow sample cannot represent all cultural variation.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 20. Why analyze both values and institutions when studying inequality?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-33-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. Values are always biologically inherited.
- B. Institutions never affect opportunities.
- C. Beliefs and organized social arrangements can interact.
- D. Only individual opinions shape outcomes.

Answer: **C**. Social outcomes involve both meaning and structure.

Objective: Demonstrate Kultura at Lipunan: Social outcomes involve both meaning and structure.

Sources: [culture](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-sociology-3e/pages/3-1-what-is-culture)

### 1. Which organization issued the State of the Global Climate 2025 report?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-01 · easy · remember

- A. World Meteorological Organization.
- B. World Trade Organization.
- C. International Maritime Organization.
- D. International Olympic Committee.
