Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): WMO publishes the climate assessment.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 2. In which year was that report published?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-02 · easy · remember

- A. 2020.
- B. 2024.
- C. 2023.
- D. 2026.

Answer: **D**. Its publication date is March 23, 2026.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Its publication date is March 23, 2026.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 3. What year is the UN's 2030 Agenda aimed at?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-03 · easy · remember

- A. 2030.
- B. 2026.
- C. 2100.
- D. 2055.

Answer: **A**. The agenda's target year is 2030.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): The agenda's target year is 2030.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 4. Which UN report was released on July 7, 2026?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-04 · easy · remember

- A. A Philippine municipal budget.
- B. The Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026.
- C. A private company's annual sales report.
- D. The State of the Global Climate 2025.

Answer: **B**. The UN report page records that launch date.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): The UN report page records that launch date.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 5. The WMO report uses which pre-industrial temperature baseline?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-05 · easy · remember

- A. 2000–2020.
- B. 1850–1900.
- C. 1700–1701.
- D. 2024–2025.

Answer: **B**. Its stated comparison uses 1850–1900.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Its stated comparison uses 1850–1900.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 6. What is a primary source for a report's official findings?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-06 · easy · remember

- A. An advertisement without a citation.
- B. The issuing agency's report.
- C. A joke account's paraphrase.
- D. An anonymous altered screenshot.

Answer: **B**. The original report directly states its findings.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): The original report directly states its findings.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 7. WMO places 2025 about 1.43°C above its baseline. What does the number describe?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-07 · medium · understand

- A. A global temperature anomaly relative to that baseline.
- B. The temperature everywhere on one day.
- C. The total temperature of the ocean.
- D. A uniform local temperature increase in every town.

Answer: **A**. An anomaly compares an average with a defined reference.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): An anomaly compares an average with a defined reference.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 8. WMO describes 2025 as second or third warmest. Why retain that qualification?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-08 · medium · apply

- A. It means the year was cold.
- B. It authorizes selecting any desired rank.
- C. It proves all measurements are useless.
- D. Different datasets can produce closely differing rankings.

Answer: **D**. The qualification preserves the reported uncertainty.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): The qualification preserves the reported uncertainty.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 9. The UN's 2026 report describes progress as uneven. What does this imply?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-09 · medium · understand

- A. All countries have identical conditions.
- B. Every target was achieved equally.
- C. Gains differ across goals and places.
- D. No gain occurred anywhere.

Answer: **C**. Uneven progress does not mean either universal success or failure.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Uneven progress does not mean either universal success or failure.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 10. A social post drops the year from a climate finding. What should be checked?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-10 · medium · apply

- A. Whether the post uses capitals.
- B. Only its number of likes.
- C. The author's avatar color.
- D. The report edition and observation period.

Answer: **D**. Dates determine what the finding describes.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Dates determine what the finding describes.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 11. Which response best evaluates a dramatic climate headline?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-11 · medium · understand

- A. Judge only the photograph.
- B. Assume all headlines are fabricated.
- C. Compare it with the original report and its definitions.
- D. Share it before reading.

Answer: **C**. Source context helps test headline accuracy.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Source context helps test headline accuracy.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 12. The UN report calls for better data access. Which action supports that aim?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-12 · medium · apply

- A. Replace data with slogans.
- B. Remove dates from tables.
- C. Hide measurement methods.
- D. Publish well-documented comparable indicators.

Answer: **D**. Transparent indicators support informed evaluation.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Transparent indicators support informed evaluation.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 13. Why distinguish the 2025 observation year from the 2026 publication year?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-13 · medium · understand

- A. Data can be analyzed and published after the period observed.
- B. They must always be identical.
- C. Publication dates establish local daily weather.
- D. Reports never use past data.

Answer: **A**. Reporting and observation periods serve different roles.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Reporting and observation periods serve different roles.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 14. WMO reports continued ocean warming. Which issue is directly relevant?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-14 · medium · apply

- A. Replacing ocean data with one inland thermometer.
- B. Ignoring marine measurements.
- C. Assuming oceans cannot store heat.
- D. Monitoring marine heat and its impacts.

Answer: **D**. Ocean observations address the reported change.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Ocean observations address the reported change.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 15. Which is a justified local application of global reporting?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-15 · medium · understand

- A. Treat a global average as each street's measurement.
- B. Assume every barangay has identical risks.
- C. Use global findings alongside local hazard and vulnerability data.
- D. Ignore local conditions.

Answer: **C**. Global and local evidence answer different questions.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Global and local evidence answer different questions.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 16. Why record a current-events question's research cutoff?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-16 · medium · apply

- A. To guarantee news never changes.
- B. Reports and verified facts can be updated.
- C. To remove the need for sources.
- D. To hide the publication date.

Answer: **B**. A cutoff makes the assessment's time context explicit.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): A cutoff makes the assessment's time context explicit.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 17. A post says a one-year anomaly permanently establishes a long-term treaty threshold. What should be examined?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Whether the author likes science.
- B. The number of exclamation marks.
- C. The threshold's time scale and the report's definitions.
- D. Only the post's font.

Answer: **C**. Annual conditions and long-term thresholds require distinct interpretation.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Annual conditions and long-term thresholds require distinct interpretation.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 18. An SDG indicator improves nationally while one region worsens. Which conclusion is sound?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. Every household improved equally.
- B. National averages can conceal unequal outcomes.
- C. The national indicator contains no information.
- D. The regional data must be impossible.

Answer: **B**. Aggregation can mask differences among groups.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Aggregation can mask differences among groups.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 19. A newer report revises an older estimate. What should a reviewer do?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Check the revised methods, coverage and uncertainty.
- B. Combine numbers without context.
- C. Always keep the older number regardless of evidence.
- D. Assume revision proves deliberate deception.

Answer: **A**. Revision can reflect improved information or methods.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Revision can reflect improved information or methods.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

### 20. Two graphs use different baselines to present warming. How should they be compared?

ID: KAT-ARALING_PANLIPUNAN-34-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. Compare bar heights without reading labels.
- B. Choose the graph with brighter colors.
- C. Align reference periods or account explicitly for the difference.
- D. Assume baseline never affects anomalies.

Answer: **C**. Different references can change displayed anomaly values.

Objective: Demonstrate Kasalukuyang Pangyayari (Current Events): Different references can change displayed anomaly values.

Sources: [sdg2026](https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2026/), [climate2025](https://public.wmo.int/publication-series/state-of-global-climate/state-of-global-climate-2025)

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 3. A barrier limits realistic options. What condition?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-03 · easy · remember

- A. Accountability
- B. Voluntariness
- C. Constraint
- D. Deliberation

Answer: **C**. Constraints restrict possibilities.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Constraints restrict possibilities.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 4. A person answers for a deliberate harmful action. What principle?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-04 · easy · remember

- A. Deliberation
- B. Voluntariness
- C. Accountability
- D. Constraint

Answer: **C**. Responsibility involves accountability.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Responsibility involves accountability.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 5. A person understands relevant options and effects before deciding. What quality?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-05 · easy · remember

- A. Coercion
- B. Informed choice
- C. Impulsiveness
- D. Reflection

Answer: **B**. Information supports meaningful choice.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Information supports meaningful choice.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 6. A threat forces apparent agreement. What issue?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-06 · easy · remember

- A. Informed choice
- B. Coercion
- C. Impulsiveness
- D. Reflection

Answer: **B**. Coercion can compromise consent.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Coercion can compromise consent.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 7. A person acts immediately without considering known risks. What pattern?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-07 · medium · understand

- A. Informed choice
- B. Impulsiveness
- C. Coercion
- D. Reflection

Answer: **B**. Impulse can bypass deliberation.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Impulse can bypass deliberation.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 8. A person reviews the reasons behind a choice. What practice?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-08 · medium · understand

- A. Reflection
- B. Coercion
- C. Informed choice
- D. Impulsiveness

Answer: **A**. Reflection evaluates conduct.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Reflection evaluates conduct.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 9. The capacity to initiate purposeful action concerns what?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-09 · medium · understand

- A. Respect for others
- B. Personal agency
- C. Social conditions
- D. Moral responsibility

Answer: **B**. Agency concerns acting intentionally.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Agency concerns acting intentionally.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 10. Recognizing that one's actions affect other people's freedom invokes what?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-10 · medium · understand

- A. Respect for others
- B. Personal agency
- C. Social conditions
- D. Moral responsibility

Answer: **A**. Others also have claims and boundaries.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Others also have claims and boundaries.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 11. Access to education changes available opportunities. What factor?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-11 · medium · understand

- A. Personal agency
- B. Respect for others
- C. Moral responsibility
- D. Social conditions

Answer: **D**. Institutions can expand or restrict choices.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Institutions can expand or restrict choices.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 12. A person deliberately breaks a justified commitment. What issue arises?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-12 · medium · understand

- A. Personal agency
- B. Social conditions
- C. Respect for others
- D. Moral responsibility

Answer: **D**. Their choice can be ethically evaluated.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Their choice can be ethically evaluated.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 13. After freely making a choice, what responsibility follows?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-13 · medium · understand

- A. Make appropriate repair
- B. Consider alternatives
- C. Accept consequences
- D. Seek reliable advice

Answer: **C**. Chosen actions can have consequences.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Chosen actions can have consequences.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 14. A careless act damages borrowed property. What response fits responsibility?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-14 · medium · understand

- A. Accept consequences
- B. Consider alternatives
- C. Make appropriate repair
- D. Seek reliable advice

Answer: **C**. Repair addresses the loss.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Repair addresses the loss.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 15. A decision involves unfamiliar serious risks. What is prudent?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-15 · medium · understand

- A. Seek reliable advice
- B. Accept consequences
- C. Consider alternatives
- D. Make appropriate repair

Answer: **A**. Relevant guidance can improve judgment.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Relevant guidance can improve judgment.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 16. A person feels trapped between two harmful choices. What should be explored?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-16 · medium · understand

- A. Make appropriate repair
- B. Consider alternatives
- C. Seek reliable advice
- D. Accept consequences

Answer: **B**. Other feasible options may exist.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Other feasible options may exist.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 17. Why does freedom not justify deliberately violating another's rights?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Freedom is not unlimited license
- B. Different constraints require examination
- C. Reduced control can affect responsibility
- D. Intent and effects both matter

Answer: **A**. Other people's freedom and dignity also matter.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Other people's freedom and dignity also matter.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 18. Why should severe coercion be considered when judging an action?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-18 · hard · analyze

- A. Different constraints require examination
- B. Intent and effects both matter
- C. Freedom is not unlimited license
- D. Reduced control can affect responsibility

Answer: **D**. Voluntariness may be restricted.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Voluntariness may be restricted.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 19. Why can two apparently identical choices involve different degrees of freedom?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Different constraints require examination
- B. Intent and effects both matter
- C. Reduced control can affect responsibility
- D. Freedom is not unlimited license

Answer: **A**. Circumstances can change realistic options.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: Circumstances can change realistic options.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

### 20. Why should a good intention not end analysis of a harmful act?

ID: KAT135-VALUES_EDUCATION-085-20 · hard · analyze

- A. Freedom is not unlimited license
- B. Reduced control can affect responsibility
- C. Different constraints require examination
- D. Intent and effects both matter

Answer: **D**. The means and consequences also require evaluation.

Objective: Demonstrate Human Freedom & Responsibility: The means and consequences also require evaluation.

Sources: [current-ve](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/9-G7-Values-Education.pdf), [current-philosophy](https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/1-1-what-is-philosophy)

## Arts, Physical Education & Health / Music Theory & Appreciation

Catalogue grades: GRADE_7, GRADE_8, GRADE_9, GRADE_10. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. How many lines are in a standard musical staff?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-01 · easy · remember

- A. Seven.
- B. Five.
- C. Six.
- D. Four.

Answer: **B**. Standard staff notation uses five lines.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Standard staff notation uses five lines.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 2. What primarily indicates how high or low a sound is?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-02 · easy · remember

- A. Dynamics.
- B. Tempo.
- C. Duration.
- D. Pitch.

Answer: **D**. Pitch describes perceived highness or lowness.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Pitch describes perceived highness or lowness.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 3. What does tempo describe?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-03 · easy · remember

- A. Loudness alone.
- B. The key signature only.
- C. The speed of the beat.
- D. Instrument size.

Answer: **C**. Tempo concerns the pace of beats.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Tempo concerns the pace of beats.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 4. What do dynamics describe?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-04 · easy · remember

- A. Staff line count.
- B. Relative loudness and softness.
- C. The composer's age.
- D. Note names only.

Answer: **B**. Dynamics shape musical intensity.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Dynamics shape musical intensity.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 5. Which symbol indicates silence for a specified duration?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-05 · easy · remember

- A. Rest.
- B. Bar line only.
- C. Sharp.
- D. Clef.

Answer: **A**. Rests indicate measured silence.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Rests indicate measured silence.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 6. What is timbre?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-06 · easy · remember

- A. Only note length.
- B. The number of staff lines.
- C. Only beat speed.
- D. Tone color or sound quality.

Answer: **D**. Timbre distinguishes sound qualities.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Timbre distinguishes sound qualities.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 7. In common notation, what does a sharp usually do to a note?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-07 · medium · understand

- A. Raises it by a semitone.
- B. Lowers it by a semitone.
- C. Makes it silent.
- D. Doubles its duration.

Answer: **A**. A sharp raises pitch relative to the natural note.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: A sharp raises pitch relative to the natural note.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 8. What does a flat usually do?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-08 · medium · apply

- A. Adds a rest.
- B. Halves tempo.
- C. Lowers a note by a semitone.
- D. Raises a note by an octave.

Answer: **C**. A flat lowers the notated pitch.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: A flat lowers the notated pitch.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 9. In 4/4 time, a quarter note normally receives how many beats?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-09 · medium · understand

- A. Two.
- B. Four.
- C. One.
- D. Three.

Answer: **C**. The lower 4 assigns the beat to the quarter note.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: The lower 4 assigns the beat to the quarter note.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 10. In 4/4 time, how many quarter-note beats complete a measure?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-10 · medium · apply

- A. Four.
- B. Two.
- C. Eight.
- D. Six.

Answer: **A**. The upper number gives four beats per measure.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: The upper number gives four beats per measure.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 11. A passage gradually becomes louder. Which term fits?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-11 · medium · understand

- A. Decrescendo.
- B. Ritardando.
- C. Staccato.
- D. Crescendo.

Answer: **D**. Crescendo indicates increasing loudness.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Crescendo indicates increasing loudness.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 12. A passage gradually becomes softer. Which term fits?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-12 · medium · apply

- A. Fortissimo.
- B. Accelerando.
- C. Decrescendo.
- D. Crescendo.

Answer: **C**. Decrescendo indicates decreasing loudness.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Decrescendo indicates decreasing loudness.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 13. The treble clef identifies which line as G?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-13 · medium · understand

- A. Bottom line as C.
- B. Second line from the bottom.
- C. Middle line as B-flat always.
- D. Top line as A.

Answer: **B**. The G clef locates G on the second staff line.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: The G clef locates G on the second staff line.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 14. A singer performs one unaccompanied melodic line. What texture is this?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-14 · medium · apply

- A. Atonal necessarily.
- B. Polyphonic necessarily.
- C. Percussive only.
- D. Monophonic.

Answer: **D**. Monophony contains one melodic line.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Monophony contains one melodic line.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 15. Two independent melodies sound together. What texture is emphasized?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-15 · medium · understand

- A. Monophonic.
- B. Silence.
- C. Unpitched speech only.
- D. Polyphonic.

Answer: **D**. Polyphony combines independent melodic lines.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Polyphony combines independent melodic lines.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 16. A familiar melody returns after a contrasting section. Which form fits A–B–A?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-16 · medium · apply

- A. Ternary.
- B. Binary only.
- C. A random sequence without return.
- D. A single repeated A section.

Answer: **A**. Ternary form returns to an opening section after contrast.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Ternary form returns to an opening section after contrast.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 17. Two instruments play the same pitch and loudness but sound different. What best explains it?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Different timbres.
- B. Different note spelling necessarily.
- C. Different silence durations.
- D. Different staff line counts.

Answer: **A**. Overtone patterns and sound production affect timbre.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Overtone patterns and sound production affect timbre.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 18. A performance is faster but not louder. Which dimension changed most directly?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. Dynamics rather than tempo.
- B. Staff notation rather than tempo.
- C. Tempo rather than dynamics.
- D. Pitch rather than tempo.

Answer: **C**. Speed and loudness are independent musical dimensions.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Speed and loudness are independent musical dimensions.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 19. Why is a single instrument insufficient to identify an entire culture's music reliably?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Each instrument belongs to only one culture forever.
- B. Instruments and traditions can overlap and change.
- C. Musical contexts never matter.
- D. All music has identical social meaning.

Answer: **B**. Context and multiple musical features support interpretation.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Context and multiple musical features support interpretation.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

### 20. Two performances use the same notes but different phrasing and dynamics. What conclusion is sound?

ID: KAT-MAPEH-40-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. Dynamics cannot affect expression.
- B. Interpretation can change expression without changing the note sequence.
- C. One must use a different alphabet.
- D. They must be identical in every audible way.

Answer: **B**. Performance choices shape musical meaning and character.

Objective: Demonstrate Music Theory & Appreciation: Performance choices shape musical meaning and character.

Sources: [music](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notation-of-notes-clefs-and-ledger-lines/), [musicrhythm](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/notating-rhythm/), [musictexture](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/texture/), [musicdynamics](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/other-aspects-of-notation/)

## Arts, Physical Education & Health / Philippine & Southeast Asian Music

Catalogue grades: GRADE_7, GRADE_8, GRADE_9, GRADE_10. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. Which tradition features a row of small tuned gongs in parts of the southern Philippines?

ID: KAT135-MAPEH-087-01 · easy · remember

- A. Kulintang
- B. Gamelan

### 19. Why consider both surrounding space and the main subject when analyzing composition?

### 20. An artwork uses realistic depth in one area and deliberate flatness elsewhere. What is the best analysis?

### 1. What is physical activity?

### 19. A team wins by breaking a safety rule. How should success be evaluated?

### 20. Why should an exercise plan consider frequency, intensity, time and type together?

- B. More of everything is always better.

### 17. A product claims natural means completely safe. What is the flaw?

- C. No health data can be studied.
- D. Confounding is impossible in nutrition.

## Business & Entrepreneurship / Entrepreneurship

Catalogue grades: GRADE_7, GRADE_8, GRADE_9, GRADE_10, GRADE_12. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. An entrepreneur primarily does what?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-01 · easy · remember

- A. Guarantees risk-free profit.
- B. Only copies a logo.
- C. Organizes resources to pursue an opportunity.
- D. Only spends without planning.

Answer: **C**. Entrepreneurship combines opportunity and resource action.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Entrepreneurship combines opportunity and resource action.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 2. What is revenue?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-02 · easy · remember

- A. A supplier's logo.
- B. Profit after all expenses.
- C. Only borrowed capital.
- D. Money earned from sales before expenses.

Answer: **D**. Revenue is sales income.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Revenue is sales income.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 3. What is profit?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-03 · easy · remember

- A. Revenue minus total cost.
- B. Revenue plus every expense.
- C. The selling price alone.
- D. Only units sold.

Answer: **A**. Profit depends on income after costs.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Profit depends on income after costs.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 4. Who is the target market?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-04 · easy · remember

- A. Only employees.
- B. The customer group a business aims to serve.
- C. Every person identically.
- D. Only tax officials.

Answer: **B**. A target market defines intended customers.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: A target market defines intended customers.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 5. What is market research?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-05 · easy · remember

- A. Guessing without evidence.
- B. Only counting office chairs.
- C. Gathering and analyzing customer and market information.
- D. Only designing packaging.

Answer: **C**. Research informs decisions about demand and competition.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Research informs decisions about demand and competition.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 6. What is a business plan?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-06 · easy · remember

- A. A structured account of goals and how to achieve them.
- B. Only a product name.
- C. A record of dreams without actions.
- D. A guarantee of success.

Answer: **A**. It connects objectives, operations and finances.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: It connects objectives, operations and finances.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

- B. A count of social-media likes.
- C. Only product weight.
- D. Total profit regardless of timing.

Answer: **A**. Timing of receipts and payments affects liquidity.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Timing of receipts and payments affects liquidity.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 12. Why record all business expenses?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-12 · medium · apply

- A. To assess true cost and profitability.
- B. To guarantee no losses.
- C. To inflate revenue.
- D. To avoid budgeting.

Answer: **A**. Missing costs distort decisions.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Missing costs distort decisions.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 13. Which is a competitive advantage?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-13 · medium · understand

- A. A hidden product defect.
- B. A copied claim with no evidence.
- C. A valuable difference customers prefer.
- D. A higher cost that offers no benefit.

Answer: **C**. Advantage must matter to customers relative to alternatives.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Advantage must matter to customers relative to alternatives.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 14. Why test a small prototype?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-14 · medium · apply

- A. To avoid feedback.
- B. To learn before committing larger resources.
- C. To replace safety checks.
- D. To guarantee universal demand.

Answer: **B**. Small tests reveal assumptions and issues.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Small tests reveal assumptions and issues.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 15. A customer reports a defect. What is responsible?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-15 · medium · understand

- A. Delete every complaint.
- B. Blame the customer automatically.
- C. Advertise the defect as a benefit.
- D. Investigate and provide an appropriate remedy.

Answer: **D**. Responsible handling supports quality and trust.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Responsible handling supports quality and trust.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 16. Which is an example of a fixed cost over a stated short period?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-16 · medium · apply

- A. Packaging for each sold item.
- B. An unchanged monthly shop rent.
- C. Material used per additional unit.
- D. Commission per item.

Answer: **B**. Fixed costs do not vary with units within the relevant range.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Fixed costs do not vary with units within the relevant range.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 17. A business has accounting profit but cannot pay a bill due today. Why?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Sales and cash are always simultaneous.
- B. Costs never require payment.
- C. Profit guarantees cash at every moment.
- D. Cash receipt and payment timing can differ from profit.

Answer: **D**. Liquidity and profitability are distinct.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Liquidity and profitability are distinct.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 18. A survey says people like a product but never asks about price. What remains uncertain?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. The owner's favorite design.
- B. Willingness and ability to buy at a viable price.
- C. Whether opinions can exist.
- D. The product's name.

Answer: **B**. Liking does not establish purchase demand.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Liking does not establish purchase demand.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 19. A higher sales volume follows both a discount and a holiday. What is the cautious interpretation?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Both factors may contribute; the discount's separate effect is uncertain.
- B. The discount alone definitely caused all growth.
- C. More sales always mean more profit.
- D. The holiday has no possible effect.

Answer: **A**. Multiple influences complicate causal attribution.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Multiple influences complicate causal attribution.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 20. Why can rapid growth threaten a small business?

ID: KAT-TLE-39-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. Growth removes every resource limit.
- B. Customers never need timely delivery.
- C. Profit automatically finances all expansion instantly.
- D. It can strain cash, staffing and production capacity.

Answer: **D**. Expansion creates operational and financing demands.

Objective: Demonstrate Entrepreneurship: Expansion creates operational and financing demands.

Sources: [business](https://openstax.org/books/entrepreneurship/pages/11-3-conducting-a-feasibility-analysis), [economics](https://openstax.org/books/principles-economics-3e/pages/3-1-demand-supply-and-equilibrium-in-markets-for-goods-and-services)

### 1. A resource controlled by a business is classified as what?

- A. Asset
- B. Liability
- C. Revenue
- D. Owner's equity

Answer: **A**. Assets provide expected economic benefits.

- C. Relevant future cash flow

Answer: **D**. It cannot be changed by the current choice.

## Research & Digital Literacy / Research Writing

Catalogue grades: GRADE_7, GRADE_8, GRADE_9, GRADE_10, GRADE_11, GRADE_12. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. What is a research question?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-01 · easy · remember

- A. A list of page margins.
- B. An unchangeable personal opinion.
- C. Only a title in bold.
- D. A focused question an investigation seeks to answer.

Answer: **D**. It directs the investigation.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: It directs the investigation.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 2. What is a citation?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-02 · easy · remember

- A. A decorative heading.
- B. An acknowledgment identifying a source.
- C. A promise that every claim is correct.
- D. A substitute for reading.

Answer: **B**. It gives credit and helps readers trace evidence.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: It gives credit and helps readers trace evidence.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 3. What is plagiarism?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-03 · easy · remember

- A. Quoting with proper attribution.
- B. Collecting data with consent.
- C. Presenting another person's work as one's own.
- D. Summarizing with a source citation.

Answer: **C**. Plagiarism conceals intellectual borrowing.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: Plagiarism conceals intellectual borrowing.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 4. What is a primary source for a student's survey study?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-04 · easy · remember

- A. A textbook summary of surveys.
- B. The student's collected survey responses.
- C. A classmate's opinion of the topic.
- D. An encyclopedia article about polls.

Answer: **B**. The original responses are direct research data.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: The original responses are direct research data.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 5. What does a bibliography or reference list identify?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-05 · easy · remember

- A. The sources used or cited.
- B. Every possible source ever published.
- C. Only the document's word count.
- D. Only the writer's classmates.

Answer: **A**. It records source information for readers.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: It records source information for readers.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 6. What is a paraphrase?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-06 · easy · remember

- A. A restatement in one's own wording with acknowledgment.
- B. A change of font only.
- C. A copied sentence without quotation marks.
- D. A list of unexplained numbers.

Answer: **A**. Paraphrasing retains meaning while changing expression and citing the source.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: Paraphrasing retains meaning while changing expression and citing the source.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

- A. What is all knowledge?

- C. How do 30 Grade 8 pupils travel to school this month?
- D. How can every world problem be solved?

Answer: **C**. It specifies a feasible population, subject and period.

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-09 · medium · understand

- A. The official text of the law.

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-10 · medium · apply

- A. Only the quotation's first word.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-11 · medium · understand

- A. So readers can judge who the findings represent.
- B. To avoid explaining limitations.

- D. To make the report look longer.

Answer: **A**. Sampling determines the scope of defensible inference.

### 12. A study surveys only basketball players about school sports. Which limitation matters?

- D. Sports preferences cannot be studied.

Answer: **C**. The sample excludes relevant groups.

### 13. Where should a methods section explain data collection?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-13 · medium · understand

- A. In an unrelated quotation.
- B. In a clear account of procedures and participants.
- C. Only in the title.
- D. Nowhere if the findings look plausible.

Answer: **B**. Transparent methods allow evaluation and replication.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: Transparent methods allow evaluation and replication.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 14. A graph uses percentages from 40 respondents. What should its caption report?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-14 · medium · apply

- A. An unrelated population total.
- B. The sample size and what the percentages measure.
- C. Only a decorative title.
- D. A guarantee of universal accuracy.

Answer: **B**. Readers need context to interpret percentages.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: Readers need context to interpret percentages.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 15. A source sells the product it praises. What should a researcher examine?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-15 · medium · understand

- A. Only its positive adjectives.
- B. Whether the article is short.
- C. Only whether its logo is attractive.
- D. Potential conflicts of interest and independent evidence.

Answer: **D**. Financial interests can influence presentation of evidence.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: Financial interests can influence presentation of evidence.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 16. What should a researcher do with findings that challenge the hypothesis?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-16 · medium · apply

- A. Claim the hypothesis was proven anyway.
- B. Change responses without disclosure.
- C. Report and examine them honestly.
- D. Delete them solely because they disagree.

Answer: **C**. Research integrity requires reporting contrary evidence.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: Research integrity requires reporting contrary evidence.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 17. Two websites repeat the same unsourced claim. Does this establish independent confirmation?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-17 · hard · analyze

- A. No; both may derive from one unverified source.
- B. Yes; two pages equal two experiments.
- C. No; websites can never contain evidence.
- D. Yes; repetition always verifies a claim.

Answer: **A**. Independence and provenance matter more than repetition.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: Independence and provenance matter more than repetition.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 18. A study finds a correlation between screen time and sleep. Which wording is justified without causal evidence?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. Sleep can never affect screen use.
- B. Screen time certainly caused every sleep problem.
- C. Screen time was associated with sleep duration in the sample.
- D. The relationship proves a treatment works.

Answer: **C**. Correlation alone does not establish causation.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: Correlation alone does not establish causation.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 19. A researcher changes the hypothesis after seeing results. What preserves transparency?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Alter the original data to match it.
- B. Omit the methods section.
- C. Pretend it was specified beforehand.
- D. Describe the change and label the new analysis exploratory.

Answer: **D**. Disclosure distinguishes exploration from prespecified testing.

Objective: Demonstrate Research Writing: Disclosure distinguishes exploration from prespecified testing.

Sources: [research](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/conducting_research/evaluating_sources_of_information/general_guidelines.html), [english](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/English-CG.pdf)

### 20. Which revision best limits an overgeneralized conclusion from one class?

ID: KAT-ENGLISH-15-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. No conclusion of any kind is possible.
- B. The class represents every country automatically.
- C. The result proves all learners behave identically.
- D. The result describes this class and warrants testing in other groups.

Answer: **D**. A qualified conclusion matches the evidence's scope.

Answer: **B**. The full account determines the amount due.

Objective: Demonstrate Food & Beverage Service: The full account determines the amount due.

Sources: [current-foodservice](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/Food-and-Beverage-Services.pdf), [current-food](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food)

### 20. A guest reports an error politely. What is the constructive response?

ID: KAT135-MISCELLANEOUS-124-20 · hard · analyze

- A. Do not assume heat removes allergens
- B. Protect guest privacy
- C. Handle complaints without blaming the guest automatically
- D. Verify the complete bill

Answer: **C**. Listen, check the facts and pursue a suitable remedy.

Objective: Demonstrate Food & Beverage Service: Listen, check the facts and pursue a suitable remedy.

Sources: [current-foodservice](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/Food-and-Beverage-Services.pdf), [current-food](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food)

## Miscellaneous / Home Economics

Catalogue grades: GRADE_7, GRADE_8, GRADE_9, GRADE_10. All 20 items: review pending.

### 1. Which practice reduces cross-contamination?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-01 · easy · remember

- A. Wipe every surface with the same dirty cloth.
- B. Separate raw and ready-to-eat foods.
- C. Store raw meat above uncovered cooked food.
- D. Use one unwashed board for everything.

Answer: **B**. Separation limits transfer of pathogens.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Separation limits transfer of pathogens.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 2. Before handling food, what should be done?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-02 · easy · remember

- A. Rinse only the utensils.
- B. Touch waste first.
- C. Wear jewelry instead of washing.
- D. Wash hands properly.

Answer: **D**. Hand hygiene reduces contamination.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Hand hygiene reduces contamination.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 3. Which is a household need rather than a discretionary want?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-03 · easy · remember

- A. Basic nutritious food.
- B. A luxury accessory.
- C. An optional game upgrade.
- D. A decorative collectible.

Answer: **A**. Basic nutrition supports essential living needs.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Basic nutrition supports essential living needs.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 4. What is a household budget?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-04 · easy · remember

- A. Only a shopping advertisement.
- B. A promise of unlimited money.
- C. A list of wishes without costs.
- D. A plan for income and expenses.

Answer: **D**. A budget allocates available funds.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: A budget allocates available funds.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 5. Which tool measures small cooking volumes?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-05 · easy · remember

- A. Measuring spoon.
- B. Colander.
- C. Spatula.
- D. Rolling pin.

Answer: **A**. Measuring spoons measure specified small volumes.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Measuring spoons measure specified small volumes.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 6. Why read a garment's care label?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-06 · easy · remember

- A. To determine its owner's age.
- B. To choose suitable cleaning and handling.
- C. To remove every stain by one method.
- D. To ignore fabric requirements.

Answer: **B**. Care instructions reflect material needs.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Care instructions reflect material needs.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 7. Raw chicken and salad are prepared. What is safest?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-07 · medium · understand

- A. Cut salad on the unwashed chicken board.
- B. Use separate cleaned equipment and prevent contact.
- C. Use chicken juices as salad dressing.
- D. Store the salad under dripping raw chicken.

Answer: **B**. Ready-to-eat food should be protected from raw-food contamination.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Ready-to-eat food should be protected from raw-food contamination.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 8. Why refrigerate perishable leftovers promptly?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-08 · medium · apply

- A. To replace cooking.
- B. To limit microbial growth.
- C. To make unsafe food permanently safe.
- D. To remove every toxin instantly.

Answer: **B**. Suitable cold storage slows many microbes.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Suitable cold storage slows many microbes.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 9. How should household expenses be prioritized when funds are limited?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-09 · medium · understand

- A. Ignore all recurring bills.
- B. Borrow without considering repayment.
- C. Meet essential needs before optional purchases.
- D. Spend everything on wants first.

Answer: **C**. Prioritization keeps spending aligned with essential needs.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Prioritization keeps spending aligned with essential needs.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 10. An item costs ₱80 each. What is the cost of three?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-10 · medium · apply

- A. ₱320.
- B. ₱160.
- C. ₱240.
- D. ₱83.

Answer: **C**. Multiply quantity by unit price.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Multiply quantity by unit price.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 11. Which shopping comparison is most useful for different package sizes?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-11 · medium · understand

- A. Shelf position alone.
- B. The biggest printed discount word.
- C. Package color only.
- D. Price per common unit of quantity.

Answer: **D**. Unit prices permit like-for-like comparison.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Unit prices permit like-for-like comparison.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 12. Why keep cleaning chemicals separate from food?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-12 · medium · apply

- A. To make containers interchangeable.
- B. To prevent chemical contamination.
- C. To improve flavor.
- D. To replace labels.

Answer: **B**. Food must be protected from toxic substances.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Food must be protected from toxic substances.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 13. Which sewing action secures a loose button appropriately?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-13 · medium · understand

- A. Stitch it firmly using suitable thread.
- B. Pull off the remaining buttons.
- C. Cut the fabric around it.
- D. Glue every buttonhole closed.

Answer: **A**. Suitable stitching restores the attachment.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Suitable stitching restores the attachment.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 14. A food package has damaged seals. What should a buyer do?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-14 · medium · apply

- A. Taste it to prove safety.
- B. Ignore all packaging integrity.
- C. Avoid using it and follow safe reporting or return procedures.
- D. Assume the contents are always safe.

Answer: **C**. A broken seal can compromise food safety.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: A broken seal can compromise food safety.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 15. Why plan meals before shopping?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-15 · medium · understand

- A. To align nutrition, quantities and budget.
- B. To guarantee every food is free.
- C. To buy every advertised item.
- D. To avoid checking existing supplies.

Answer: **A**. Planning reduces waste and supports balanced purchases.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Planning reduces waste and supports balanced purchases.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 16. Which storage practice is appropriate?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-16 · medium · apply

- A. Store all foods at the same temperature indefinitely.
- B. Mix chemicals with ingredients.
- C. Remove every date label.
- D. Keep foods protected, labeled and under suitable conditions.

Answer: **D**. Conditions and traceability support safe storage.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Conditions and traceability support safe storage.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 17. A discounted large pack spoils before use. Was it necessarily economical?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-17 · hard · analyze

- A. Yes; spoilage has no cost.
- B. No; every discount is dishonest.
- C. No; usable quantity and waste affect actual value.
- D. Yes; larger packs always save money.

Answer: **C**. Waste can outweigh a low unit price.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Waste can outweigh a low unit price.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 18. A reheated food was left warm for a long period. Why can reheating alone be insufficient?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-18 · hard · evaluate

- A. Smell always detects every hazard.
- B. Heat never affects microbes.
- C. All food becomes sterile merely by stirring.
- D. Some hazards or toxins may persist despite reheating.

Answer: **D**. Unsafe storage cannot always be corrected by reheating.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Unsafe storage cannot always be corrected by reheating.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 19. Two meals cost the same but differ in nutrients. What is the better comparison?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-19 · hard · analyze

- A. Choose only by plate color.
- B. Assume equal cost means equal nutrition.
- C. Assess nutritional balance as well as cost.
- D. Ignore dietary needs.

Answer: **C**. Cost alone does not determine dietary quality.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Cost alone does not determine dietary quality.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)

### 20. A family repeatedly exceeds its budget. What is the best first analysis?

ID: KAT-TLE-36-20 · hard · evaluate

- A. Compare recorded actual expenses with planned categories.
- B. Assume income is unlimited.
- C. Guess without reviewing records.
- D. Eliminate every essential purchase immediately.

Answer: **A**. Records reveal where the plan and actual spending differ.

Objective: Demonstrate Home Economics: Records reveal where the plan and actual spending differ.

Sources: [food](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639), [foodpractice](https://www.who.int/activities/promoting-safe-food-handling/five-key-to-safer-food), [tle](https://www.deped.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EPP-CG.pdf)
